### `ClientInfo` (message)

Direction: the PHONE is the server. It advertises `_imuninn._tcp` over Bonjour and listens for control (WebSocket), data-TCP connections; clients (PCs) connect. A client opens the control WebSocket and sends Hello; the phone answers Welcome.

| field | type | # | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | e.g. hostname or script name |
| `version` | `string` | 2 | client library version |

| field | type | # | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | `ClientInfo` | 1 |  |
| `udp_port` | `uint32` | 2 | where this client receives DataMessage datagrams (0 = none) |
| `protocol_version` | `uint32` | 3 |  |
| `data_transport` | `Transport` | 4 | v5: how this client wants its data streams. TCP (default) = the length-prefixed stream on Welcome.tcp_port plus UDP for pose / IMU / health when udp_port > 0. WEBSOCKET = the client opens a second WebSocket to the control port and sends "IMDATA01" + uint32 LE client_id as its first binary frame; the phone then sends every subscribed stream (video, depth, pose, IMU, health) on it as binary DataMessage frames. Browsers use this; nothing else changes. |

Image orientation: ARKit captured images are sensor-native landscape and do not rotate with the device (§5.4). `rotation_deg` says how to rotate to make the image upright for display; data is always sent as captured. `rotation_deg`: rotate the image clockwise by this much to view it upright when the phone is held in portrait. On iPhone, every camera (back lenses and the front camera) delivers landscape sensor frames that need 90; the field exists so other devices can say otherwise. Intrinsics are in the sensor frame.

| `keyframe` | `bool` | 5 |  |
| `data` | `bytes` | 6 | v1: payload inline (§6.1) |
| `intrinsics` | `Intrinsics` | 7 |  |
| `rotation_deg` | `uint32` | 8 | 0 / 90 / 180 / 270 |
